title: Apostol takes over as new Philippine Marine Corps Commandant
summary: Brigadier General Bob Apostol on Monday formally assumed the role of Commandant of the Philippine Marine Corps (PMC) during a change of command ceremony at Marine Barracks Rudiardo Brown in Fort…

blocks.text: Brigadier General Bob Apostol on Monday formally assumed the role of Commandant of the Philippine Marine Corps (PMC) during a change of command ceremony at Marine Barracks Rudiardo Brown in Fort Bonifacio, Taguig City.
In a statement, the PMC said the ceremony was presided over by Philippine Navy Flag Officer in Command Vice Admiral Jose Ma. Ambrosio Ezpeleta.

Apostol succeeded Brigadier General Bayani Curaming as PMC Commandant through the formal relinquishment and assumption of command, turnover of the command symbol, and his installation as the Marines’ new head.
In his assumption remarks, Apostol said he wants to continue the Marines’ direction while calling for further improvements in its capabilities amid an evolving security environment.
“This change of command does not mean a change of direction. We inherit what others have built; we must improve it and hand over a force better than we found it,” Apostol said.
He also reaffirmed PMC’s identity as the “Nation's Force of Choice,” anchored on its values of Karangalan, Katungkulan, at Kabayanihan.
Apostol said the PMC would continue developing multi-capable Marine forces for archipelagic coastal defense while embracing the Fleet-Marine concept and maintaining its naval character.
He also underscored the need for agility and resilience in responding to emerging threats, as well as the importance of looking after the welfare of Marines.

“We must be agile to adapt to evolving threats. We will embrace resilience, enduring, recovering, and growing stronger. Above all, we will uphold the welfare of every Marine, for they are the heart of this force,” he said.
For his part, Ezpeleta outlined three key responsibilities for Apostol as he takes the helm of the PMC: strengthening the institution, preparing the force, and ensuring the welfare of its personnel.
“As you assume command, I entrust you with three important responsibilities: strengthen the institution, prepare the force, and take care of our Marines,” Ezpeleta said.
“These are interconnected responsibilities that will ensure the Corps remains strong, ready, and capable of fulfilling its mission,” he added. —Joviland Rita/RF, GMA News
